English: Stone Bench
A simple stone bench, hewn from local rock, serves as both a workspace and symbol of the first settled artisans in the wild frontier. It marks the beginning of organized stonework among the nomads.
Carvers Hut
A crude shelter of timber and thatch houses the first dedicated stone carvers, increasing efficiency and attracting craftspeople to the growing camp.
Stone Cutter Room
A sturdier structure built of stone and wood, providing space for multiple artisans and allowing for more sophisticated stonework, further boosting the camps productivity.
Patterned Workshop
A semi-permanent stone and adobe workshop, adorned with basic patterns, where skilled artisans coordinate decoration and advanced stonework, enhancing the camps prestige and unity.
Fine Carving Pavilion
A grand pavilion with intricate stonework, reserved for master artisans. Its presence inspires the clan, increases population, and attracts renowned craftsmen from afar.
Master Carver Hall
A prestigious stone hall, home to the most skilled carvers. It serves as a center for artisan training and innovation, strengthening the hordes logistical backbone.
Artisans Chamber
A lavish chamber reserved for the most talented artisans, providing a hub for innovation and coordination of major stoneworks across the hordes territory.
Guild Pavilion
A monumental tented pavilion where guilds of Mesoamerican stoneworkers gather. This structure fosters unity, coordination, and logistical excellence for the nomad horde.
Grand Stone Hall
The Grand Stone Hall stands as a testament to Mesoamerican mastery, a permanent and magnificently adorned center of administration and unity for the nomad clan.
Mesoamerican Stone Guild
A legendary guild, bringing together all master artisans, planners, and stoneworkers under one roof. It is the ultimate symbol of Mesoamerican nomad strength and organization.
